title: One Touch Switch: Changing Broadband Made Easy
description: One Touch Switch lets your new UK broadband provider handle the whole switch, even between networks like Openreach, Virgin Media and altnets. How it works.
h1: One Touch Switch: how switching broadband works now
intro: Switching broadband between different networks used to mean calling your old provider and juggling dates. With One Touch Switch, your new provider does it for you.

image.alt: Person holding a smartphone while working at a desk

sections.html: Ofcom required broadband and landline providers to support a “gaining provider-led” switching process across all fixed networks. It went live in September 2024, so you can now switch between, say, an Openreach-based provider, Virgin Media and a full fibre altnet without contacting your old provider first.

1. Choose your new provider and order.
  2. Give your name, address and current provider (some may ask for an account number).
  3. Your new provider contacts the old one and sends you details of any exit fees or effects on other services.
  4. The switch happens on the agreed date; your old contract ends automatically.

• You shouldn’t pay notice period charges after your switch date.
  • You get clear information on any early exit fees before you commit.
  • Providers in Ofcom’s automatic compensation scheme pay out if a switch is delayed or an engineer misses an appointment.
